source_caption:
The Covenant — A Promise Under Fire

Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant (2023) follows Sergeant John Kinley, a U.S. Army soldier whose unit is ambushed during a mission in Afghanistan. When the situation turns deadly, Kinley survives largely because of Ahmed, a local interpreter who risks his own life to save him.

After returning home, Kinley discovers that Ahmed and his family are still in danger and that the promise he made to protect him has not been fulfilled. Determined to repay the debt, Kinley returns to Afghanistan to find Ahmed and bring him to safety.

The mission becomes deeply personal as Kinley realizes the risks Ahmed took for him and his fellow soldiers. With limited time and dangerous forces standing in their way, Kinley must rely on determination and courage to keep his promise.

The film explores themes of loyalty, sacrifice, friendship, courage, and keeping one's word. It highlights the bond that can develop between people who depend on each other in life-or-death situations.

What makes The Covenant compelling is the emotional connection between Kinley and Ahmed combined with intense military action. At its heart, the story is about one man refusing to abandon someone who once saved his life.

💬 He survived because Ahmed saved him—now he's going back to keep his promise.

source_details.synopsis: Guy Ritchie's The Covenant (or simply The Covenant) is a 2023 American action drama film produced and directed by Guy Ritchie and co-written with Marn Davies and Ivan Atkinson. The film stars Jake Gyllenhaal and Dar Salim. Its plot follows John Kinley, a U.S. Army Green Beret Master Sergeant sent home after surviving a Taliban ambush and a harrowing trek to safety, and his subsequent journey to rescue Ahmed, his Afghan interpreter, whom John feels indebted to for saving his life. The film was theatrically released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and STXfilms in the United States on April 21, 2023, received generally positive reviews from critics and grossed $21 million.
